briefing.text: On Nov 26, Information Technology stayed No. 1 in sector attention on all three platforms: News buzz 83.7 (-1.6 on the day, -1.3 on the week, mentions -59%, sentiment 0.09), X 93.4 (-0.3, +0.4 on the week, mentions -2%, sentiment 0.11) and Reddit 93.3 (-0.9, -1.8 on the week, mentions -50%, sentiment -0.01), with NVDA, MU and AMD among the top tickers. On News, Real Estate fell to 73.7 (-4.2, -0.4 on the week, mentions -44%, sentiment 0.18; O, PLD, EQIX) and Utilities to 68.1 (-4.1, -4.8 on the week, mentions -42%, sentiment 0.05; DUK, EIX, AEP). On X, Utilities rose to 84.0 (+2.0, +3.9 on the week, mentions +248%, sentiment 0.08; FLNC, PPL, NFE) and Energy to 88.8 (+1.8, +2.8 on the week, mentions +175%, sentiment 0.11; VVV, FET, CVX), while Healthcare dropped to 41.3 (-20.7, -27.1 on the week, mentions -76%, sentiment 0.18; MEDS, ASPE, BLSM). On Reddit, Technology jumped to 36.6 (+12.9, still -18.8 on the week, mentions +200%, sentiment 0.03; AZIO) and Utilities rose to 76.8 (+5.3, +1.2 on the week, mentions +6%, sentiment 0.07; AES, NEE, RWE).

IOT (#1): a stock-list mention and a piece on its four profitable quarters; general coverage that does not by itself explain the rank.
URBN (#2): shares broke below the 50-day average after an analyst downgrade; this is negative coverage and does not clearly explain the attention jump.
MO (#3): Altria confirmed it is considering a likely all-cash bid for Imperial Brands; this is a clear driver of its attention.
DLTR (#4): a report of a 3% stock fall and a piece on the business after the Family Dollar sale; it fits the price move only in part.
LYFT (#5): a piece on Uber's bookings and a fund's larger Lyft stake; neither clearly explains the rank.
DPZ (#7): valuation commentary and a China supply chain expansion story; only a partial explanation.
CMCSA (#9): the headlines shown are about an investor's dividend buys and a Liberty Global rally; they do not explain the rank.
PLTR (#10): commentary on speculative AI stocks and Big Tech rivals; heavy coverage (70 articles in 2 days) but no single event in these headlines.

IOT is #1 (score 0.939, up from #5): its price move of 2.18 times normal daily volatility is in the 99th percentile, with attention (98th), attention on X (98th) and volume (94th) also high, and earnings due 12-03. URBN is #2 (0.895, not ranked in the previous pull): attention (96th percentile), attention on X (97th) and volume (96th) are high, momentum is more moderate (79th), and no catalyst is listed. MO is #3 (0.873, down from #2): attention is the highest of scored topics (100th percentile) and X attention is 99th, with volume 86th and a KPI market resolving as the catalyst. MO's momentum is low (20th percentile, price +0.4% over 24h).
